title: Cleave a 30 mm test piece off a silicon wafer: scribe a short nick at the tick, then break it with cleaving pliers
instruction: Cleave this wafer at the tick on its rim to cut off a 30 mm wide test piece. With the diamond scriber, scribe a short nick at the tick, no more than 5 mm in from the rim. Then break the wafer from the nick with the cleaving pliers. Touch the wafer only with the scriber's tip and the pliers' jaws, and leave both pieces on the stage.
context: Process engineers and technicians in nanofabs and chip process-development and failure-analysis labs cut wafers into test pieces by hand for etch, deposition and lithography trials and cross-sections: "The cleaving process is commonly performed by scribing the wafer surface with a diamond scribe, then breaking the wafer" (Cleanroom Technology, 2019); "An initiation scribe is a short scribe made at one edge of the substrate ... it will break following the crystal plane", best with "3-point loading pliers ... used as close to the edge as possible" (SPI Supplies technical note, 2018). The difficulty is physical: too light a scribe leaves no nick and the pliers then shatter the wafer; too hard chips it; too far in scratches the polished face; pliers off the nick shatter it. The crack follows the {110} plane by itself, so crystal orientation is not judged. The wafer is touched only by the tools: fingers mark the face and cleaved edges are sharp. The pocket stage stands in for the technician's steadying fingertip, like the stops of commercial scribing stages. The simulation's force thresholds (scribe 0.3 to 3 N, chip 3 to 6 N, cleave 12 N at the jaw ridge from a nick, 24 N without) are fracture-mechanics estimates; a kitchen-scale bench check in the README confirms them on the real rig.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart at the table's near edge), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Nothing is random. Tray: black polypropylene lab tray, 30 x 40 cm inside, 2.5 cm walls, 3 mm floor, its 40 cm sides along y: inside x 31 to 61, y -20 to +20. Stage (fixed in the tray): a 6 cm round PETG column, 10.9 cm tall, under a 12 cm round, 8 mm thick PETG plate centred at (46, -2), top 12.0 cm up. A 0.25 mm polyester shim (0.5 mm in the simulation, for the wafer drawn 1 mm thick) on the plate with a cut-out of the wafer's outline plus 0.3 mm (flat included) forms the pocket. A notch 40 mm wide (y -1.5 to +2.5) is cut through the plate from its near edge to x 42.42, so the wafer's rim overhangs 10 mm there; it leaves 24 mm of side play for the jaws. Two PETG hold-down tabs on the plate's far rim, 35 degrees either side of +x from the wafer's centre, each 10 mm wide with a lip reaching 1.5 mm over the rim 0.2 mm above the face, keep the far rim down when the scriber presses on the overhang. Wafer: silicon, 100 mm, (100), p-type, single-side polished test grade, polished face up, 9.5 g (525 um; drawn 1 mm thick). SEMI M1 32.5 mm primary flat facing the robot along y at x 41.27, from y -3.6 to -0.4; centre (46, -2). A black tick 4 mm long and 0.6 mm wide runs along the target line in from the rim at (41.42, 0); the target cleave line runs along x at y 0, so the coupon is the 30 mm piece left of it. Scriber: pen-style diamond scriber (Electron Microscopy Sciences 62107-ST), aluminium barrel 9 mm across and 140 mm long, brass collet cone, 15 g. It stands point down in an 11 mm square hole, 25 mm deep, in the top of a blue PLA stand 4 x 4 x 12.5 cm at (36.6, -25) outside the tray; its point rests 10.0 cm up. Pliers: 6 in (152 mm) wafer-cleaving pliers with 3-point plastic jaws (SPI CleanBreak 07649-AB or Ted Pella CleanBreak 54361), steel, 120 g. Jaws 16 mm wide across the cleave line and 10 mm long, 18 to 28 mm in front of the pivot; the lower jaw has a 1 mm ridge along its centre, the upper jaw two 2 mm pads 6 mm either side. Red vinyl grips 32 x 12 x 10 mm at the handle ends, centred 108 mm behind the pivot (lever ratio about 4). The supplier's 0.75 in maximum opening is limited at rest by a nylon cord loop round the grips: jaws 6 mm open, grips 50 mm apart centre to centre (60 mm over their outsides); the cord goes slack when squeezed. Return spring 6 N at the grips at rest, about 8 N closed onto a wafer. They lie on edge (pivot axis along y), jaws toward +x, pivot at (46.8, 7.5) 12.0 cm up, jaw tips at x 49.6, grip ends at x 34.4, on a grey PLA stand in the tray: two slotted posts (16 mm long, 30 mm wide, 20 mm slot between 12 mm walls) on a 100 x 40 x 4 mm base; the front post (x 47.0 to 48.6) carries the jaw arms on its slot floor 10.95 cm up, the rear post (x 40.0 to 41.6) the lower handle on its floor 9.73 cm up. Printable files are in cad/: STL for the stage (plate, column, hold-down tabs), both stands and the tick gauge, and an SVG of the shim's cut lines. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: Real-trial tools: overhead and side video, caliper (0.1 mm), steel ruler with 0.5 mm marks, 10x loupe, low-angle LED lamp. A piece is a fragment 3 mm or larger across; smaller fragments (a chip's) are ignored in every tier and in the shattered latch. Latched 0 at any time: (1) a gripper finger touches the wafer or a piece (video, or a fingerprint on the face under the lamp); (2) anything other than the scriber's diamond tip, the pliers' jaw inserts or the stage's hold-down tabs touches the wafer's top face (video); (3) scratch: a visible line 1 mm or longer more than 5 mm in from the rim (sim: in one stroke the tip slides 1 mm or more at 0.3 N or more there); (4) shattered: three or more pieces (sim: also a scribe force over 6 N, 24 N or more on the jaw ridge with no nick within 3 mm of its line, or the scriber, the pliers or a gripper first touching the wafer at over 0.3 m/s); (5) a piece leaves the stage (more than 5 mm below its top) or turns face down. Gate for any positive score: both grippers' fingertips 3 cm or more from every piece, the pliers and the scriber off the wafer, every piece still (under 1 mm/s), all for 1 s (the last second of video); the score is the last reading taken under the gate, 0 if the gate never holds. Nick: a scribe line 1 mm or longer reaching the rim and lying wholly within 5 mm of it (sim: a tip stroke of that kind at 0.3 to 6 N that ends within 1 mm of the rim or runs off it). Chip: a missing piece 1 mm or more across at the nick end of the cleaved edge (sim: the cleaving nick was scribed at 3 to 6 N). Cleaved from the nick (needed for every two-piece score): a nick lies along the cleaved edge at its rim end (sim: the wafer is cut only on the pre-cut line nearest a recorded nick's rim end). Coupon width: caliper, perpendicular to the cleaved edge, to the coupon's farthest rim point; target 30.0 mm. 1.0: exactly two pieces, cleaved from the nick, flat (tilted 5 degrees or less) and face up on the stage, width 29.0 to 31.0 mm, no chip. 0.75: two pieces cleaved from the nick, width 28.0 to 32.0 mm. 0.5: two pieces cleaved from the nick, width 26.0 to 34.0 mm. 0.25: the wafer uncut, with a nick whose rim end is within 3 mm of the tick. Otherwise 0, including any break not from a nick. Sim forces are averaged over each 50 ms control step: the scribe force and touches are PhysX contact forces; the jaw ridge's force is the pliers' clamp, the holding gripper's squeeze less the return spring times the lever (108/25.3 mm), counted while the jaws are at their closing stop on the wafer.
reset_notes: One new 100 mm test-grade wafer per trial (about US$11). Lay it in the pocket, polished face up, flat toward the robot; draw the tick with an ultra-fine marker through the slot of a printed gauge laid on the wafer, flat to flat. Stand the scriber back in its stand and lay the pliers back on theirs with the cord loop on. Pieces go in a sharps container; clear fragments with tape or a brush. Staff wear safety glasses and nitrile gloves. Each gripper pad wears a replaceable cover of 1 in polyimide tape (3M 5413); after any trial in which a finger touched silicon, replace the cover and check the pad for shards. Jaw inserts are replaceable (a spare 3-point set comes with the SPI pair; for the Ted Pella pair, confirm the 3-point set when ordering replacement jaws). About 3 minutes per reset; all kit under US$250.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; fracture is a rule: the wafer is one body until it fires, then is swapped in place for two pieces pre-cut on the {110} line nearest the nick (1 mm grid). A tip stroke of 1 mm or more within 5 mm of the rim, reaching it, at 0.3-3 N nicks; 3-6 N chips; over 6 N shatters. The jaw clamp is the gripper's squeeze through the lever; a closing stop at the wafer's drawn thickness (1 mm, real mass) stands in for its stiffness. 12 N within 3 mm of a nick cleaves; 24 N with no nick shatters.
